title: Booking calendar with half-open intervals
prompt: Build an in-memory HTTP booking calendar. Resource names match [a-z0-9-]{1,40}. POST /resources/:resource/bookings accepts a JSON body with exactly start and end, both ISO 8601 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset, for example 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z or 2026-03-01T12:00:00+02:00 (fractional seconds allowed). A timestamp without an offset, an unparseable value, end not strictly after start, a bad resource name, extra fields or malformed JSON returns 400. Bookings are half-open intervals [start,end) compared as instants, so offsets do not matter and a booking that ends exactly when another starts does not overlap it. A booking overlapping an existing active booking of the same resource returns 409 and changes nothing; other resources are independent. Success returns 201 {id,resource,start,end} with start and end normalized to UTC in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ and id a unique nonempty string. DELETE /bookings/:id returns 204 with no body and frees the interval, or 404 for an unknown ID. GET /resources/:resource/bookings returns 200 {items} with active bookings ordered by start instant, then by creation order; an unknown resource returns an empty list. Concurrent competing requests must never create overlapping bookings. No persistence or external services are needed.
